raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Pipeline-parallelism is a foundational paradigm for serving large models efficiently. However, currently, multi-LoRA serving does not handle PP in the most efficient way possible, both in terms of throughput and GPU memory usage.

#### Example

Consider PP=2, with 4 slots on each GPU. Microbatch A uses 2 adapters, and the scheduler is building microbatch B from requests for 3 other adapters. Both microbatches pass through both GPUs, but each GPU only considers the adapters of its own microbatch. Since B's 3 adapters fit in 4 slots on their own, the scheduler admits all of B's requests, even though A and B together need 5. Every GPU then evicts and loads adapters on every step as A and B take turns. With this PR, each GPU keeps the adapters of all in-flight micro-batches loaded, and the scheduler only admits a request if its adapter fits alongside them. B gets 2 of its 3 adapters, and the request for the third waits until a slot frees up.

```
main
  Stage 0 │▒ load ▒▒█ run A █│▒ load ▒▒█ run B █│▒ load ▒▒█ run A █│▒ load ▒▒█ run B █│
  Stage 1 │                  │▒ load ▒▒█ run A █│▒ load ▒▒█ run B █│▒ load ▒▒█ run A █│▒ load ▒▒█ run B █│

branch
  Stage 0 │▒ load ▒▒█ run A █│▒ load ▒▒█ run B █│█ run A █│█ run B █│
  Stage 1 │                  │▒ load ▒▒█ run A █│█ run B █│█ run A █│█ run B █│

█ compute   ▒ load adapters
```

## Modifications

There are two main modifications that I made:
- `LoRAManager`s on a given PP stage should prioritize keeping adapters that are needed in other stages in the memory pool. Previously, `LoRAManager`s were only aware of the adapters needed for their own next microbatch.
- Each stage's LoRA memory pool only allocates adapter weights for the layers that stage uses, which reduces the GPU memory per adapter slot by a factor of the PP size.

## Accuracy Tests

- Added a new unit test for PP LoRA
- All LoRA tests pass

## Speed Tests and Profiling

I benchmarked on 2xH200s on a single node. To benchmark throughput and memory improvements for `main` and my branch:

1. Start the server:

```
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct \
    --pp-size 2 \
    --enable-lora \
    --max-loaded-loras 16 \
    --max-loras-per-batch 8 \
    --lora-paths \
        adapter0=advy/llama71b-mentalchat16k \
        adapter1=advy/llama71b-career-guidance \
        adapter2=clembench-playpen/llama-3.1-70B-Instruct_playpen_SFT_DFINAL_0.6K-steps \
        adapter3=reissbaker/r1-llama-70b-distill-lora \
        adapter4=kushwanth7/llama-70b-manim-lora \
        adapter5=kmtao/llama3.1-70B-HIVDB-adapter \
        adapter6=cosmicishan/llama-70b-mcq-dlgenai \
        adapter7=impactIA/chimere \
        adapter8=dv347/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-honly \
        adapter9=cyborgwittgenstein/cassie-70b-v7-lora \
        adapter10=eac123/MarcusChenHolloway-70B-LoRA \
        adapter11=hf-100/Llama-3.1-Spellbound-StoryWriter-70b-instruct-0.2-lora \
        adapter12=Strike0010/hs-classifier-70b-dpo-iter2-arm1 \
        adapter13=ReflexxIA/reflexx-70b-v1 \
        adapter14=Boffl/BullingerLM-llama3.1-70B-instruct-qa \
        adapter15=gane5hvarma/joe-adapter
```

2. Run a benchmark where there are more adapters being served than slots in the memory pool:

```
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \
    --backend sglang \
    --base-url http://localhost:30000 \
    --dataset-name random \
    --num-prompts 400 \
    --max-concurrency 32 \
    --random-input-len 512 \
    --random-output-len 512 \
    --lora-request-distribution uniform \
    --lora-name \
        adapter0 \
        adapter1 \
        adapter2 \
        adapter3 \
        adapter4 \
        adapter5 \
        adapter6 \
        adapter7 \
        adapter8 \
        adapter9 \
        adapter10 \
        adapter11 \
        adapter12 \
        adapter13 \
        adapter14 \
        adapter15
```

#### Throughput Results

| Metric | `main` | PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Benchmark duration (s) | 2,370.2 | 420.1 | **−82.3%** |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 44.3 | 250.2 | **5.6×** |
| Mean E2E latency (ms) | 187,553 | 31,353 | **−83.3%** |
| Median E2E latency (ms) | 189,043 | 30,307 | **−84.0%** |
| P99 E2E latency (ms) | 404,723 | 79,866 | **−80.3%** |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 709.4 | 77.0 | **−89.1%** |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 722.3 | 77.0 | **−89.3%** |
| P99 TPOT (ms) | 928.4 | 87.8 | **−90.5%** |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 2,601 | 11,196 | +330% |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 854 | 2,341 | +174% |
| P99 TTFT (ms) | 33,987 | 47,861 | +41% |

The scheduler now admits a request only when its adapter fits alongside those of in-flight micro-batches, instead of evicting adapters that are still in use. Thus, new requests may wait longer for a slot (resulting in higher TTFT), but no longer cause reloads on every decode step, resulting in a much lower TPOT.

#### Memory Results

```
main
[2026-10-23 01:40:28 PP1] KV Cache is allocated. dtype: torch.bfloat16, #tokens: 295680, K size: 22.56 GB, V size: 22.56 GB
[2026-10-23 01:40:28 PP0] KV Cache is allocated. dtype: torch.bfloat16, #tokens: 295680, K size: 22.56 GB, V size: 22.56 GB
[2026-10-23 01:40:28 PP1] Memory pool end. avail mem=13.94 GB
[2026-10-23 01:40:28 PP0] Memory pool end. avail mem=11.99 GB

branch
[2026-10-23 01:30:51 PP0] KV Cache is allocated. dtype: torch.bfloat16, #tokens: 337562, K size: 25.75 GB, V size: 25.75 GB
[2026-10-23 01:30:51 PP1] KV Cache is allocated. dtype: torch.bfloat16, #tokens: 337562, K size: 25.75 GB, V size: 25.75 GB
[2026-10-23 01:30:51 PP0] Memory pool end. avail mem=11.98 GB
[2026-10-23 01:30:51 PP1] Memory pool end. avail mem=13.94 GB
```

So you can see that the branch has ~40k more tokens free for the KV cache on each stage, which correctly equates to saving half of an adapter for 8 adapters for this model.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -17,7 +17,7 @@ The following server arguments are relevant for multi-LoRA serving:
 
 * `lora_paths`: The list of LoRA adapters to load. Each adapter must be specified in one of the following formats: <PATH> | <NAME>=<PATH> | JSON with schema {"lora_name":str,"lora_path":str,"pinned":bool}.
 
-* `max_loras_per_batch`: Maximum number of adaptors used by each batch. This argument can affect the amount of GPU memory reserved for multi-LoRA serving, so it should be set to a smaller value when memory is scarce. Defaults to be 8.
+* `max_loras_per_batch`: GPU pool capacity in distinct adapter IDs, including `None` for base-model requests. With pipeline parallelism, this capacity is shared across all in-flight microbatches. More slots reserve more GPU memory. Defaults to 8.
 
 * `max_loaded_loras`: If specified, it limits the maximum number of LoRA adapters loaded in CPU memory at a time. The value must be greater than or equal to `max-loras-per-batch`.
 
@@ -412,6 +412,14 @@ server_process, port = launch_server_cmd(
 terminate_process(server_process)
 ```
 
+## LoRA with pipeline parallelism
+
+With `--pp-size > 1`, each stage shares its LoRA GPU pool across all in-flight microbatches. `--max-loras-per-batch` limits the union of their adapter IDs, including one slot for `None` when base-model requests are present.
+
+Each stage allocates transformer-layer LoRA buffers only for its local modules. For balanced partitions of homogeneous layers at the same slot count and LoRA rank, these buffers use approximately `1 / pp_size` of their unpartitioned size per stage. Embedding and output-head buffers follow the LoRA-enabled modules present on each stage. This ratio does not describe total GPU memory usage. You can increase `--max-loras-per-batch` if your actual GPU memory budget permits.
+
+When requests target more adapters than fit in the pool, requests for additional adapters wait for a slot. To improve fairness under skewed traffic, set [`--lora-drain-wait-threshold`](/docs/advanced_features/lora#arguments-for-lora-serving) to a positive value. Its default, `0`, disables draining.
+
 ## LoRA with DP attention
 
 SGLang supports LoRA serving with [data parallel attention (DPA)](/docs/advanced_features/dp_dpa_smg_guide). The model architecture must support DPA, and you must currently select the Triton LoRA backend. Other built-in LoRA backends reject this configuration at startup.

+def _req(lora_id, finished=False):
+    return SimpleNamespace(lora_id=lora_id, finished=lambda: finished)
+
+
+def _batch(*reqs):
+    return SimpleNamespace(reqs=list(reqs))
+
+
+def _lora_manager(slots):
+    pool = LoRAMemoryPool.__new__(LoRAMemoryPool)
+    pool.max_loras_per_batch = slots
+    pool.uid_to_buffer_id = {}
+    pool.buffer_id_to_uid = [EMPTY_SLOT] * slots
+    pool.eviction_policy = get_eviction_policy("lru")
+    pool.load_lora_weight_to_buffer = lambda *_args: None
+
+    manager = LoRAManager.__new__(LoRAManager)
+    manager.max_loras_per_batch = slots
+    manager.memory_pool = pool
+    manager.num_pinned_loras = 0
+    manager.loras = {}
+    manager.lora_refs = {}
+    manager.lora_modules = []
+    manager.embed_tokens_module = None
+    manager.lm_head_module = None
+    return manager
+
+
+class TestAllPPLoras(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_covers_every_micro_batch_except_finished_requests(self):
+        """A launched prefill not yet merged into its decode batch still counts;
+        requests that finished before their micro-batch's next turn do not."""
+        scheduler = Scheduler.__new__(Scheduler)
+        decoding, base, launched = _req("decoding"), _req(None), _req("launched")
+        scheduler.running_mbs = [
+            _batch(decoding, _req("decoding", finished=True)),
+            _batch(base),
+        ]
+        scheduler.mbs = [_batch(launched), None]
+        self.assertCountEqual(
+            map(id, scheduler._get_all_pp_reqs()), map(id, [decoding, base, launched])
+        )
+
+        scheduler.enable_lora = True
+        scheduler.tp_worker = SimpleNamespace(
+            model_runner=SimpleNamespace(lora_manager=_lora_manager(slots=4))
+        )
+        reporter = SchedulerMetricsReporter.__new__(SchedulerMetricsReporter)
+        reporter.scheduler = scheduler
+        reporter.stats = SimpleNamespace()
+        with get_parallel().override(pp_size=2):
+            reporter._update_lora_metrics()
+        self.assertEqual(
+            (
+                reporter.stats.lora_pool_slots_used,
+                reporter.stats.lora_pool_slots_total,
+                reporter.stats.lora_pool_utilization,
+            ),
+            (2, 4, 0.5),
+        )
+
+    @mock.patch("time.monotonic", return_value=100.0)
+    def test_draining_uses_all_micro_batches(self, _clock):
+        def request(lora_id, max_new_tokens):
+            req = _req(lora_id)
+            req.sampling_params = SimpleNamespace(max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens)
+            req.output_ids = []
+            req.is_retracted = False
+            req.time_stats = SimpleNamespace(wait_queue_entry_time=0.0)
+            return req
+
+        short, long = request("short", 5), request("long", 100)
+        waiting = request("waiting", 100)
+        first, second = _batch(short), _batch(long)
+        for batch in (first, second):
+            batch.batch_is_full = False
+            batch.is_empty = lambda: False
+
+        # Stop after LoRA admission setup, before allocating or running a prefill.
+        adder = SimpleNamespace(
+            can_run_list=[], preempt_list=[], budget_state=lambda: AddReqResult.OTHER
+        )
+        scheduler = Scheduler.__new__(Scheduler)
+        scheduler.__dict__.update(
+            running_mbs=[first, second],
+            mbs=[first, second],
+            waiting_queue=[waiting],
+            lora_drainer=LoRADrainer(max_loras_per_batch=2, max_wait_time_secs=3),
+            enable_lora=True,
+            enable_lora_overlap_loading=False,
+            enable_priority_preemption=False,
+            is_hybrid_swa=False,
+            chunked_req=None,
+            min_free_slots_delayer=None,
+            is_mixed_chunk=False,
+            dllm_config=None,
+            grammar_manager=SimpleNamespace(has_waiting_grammars=lambda: False),
+            policy=mock.Mock(),
+            processed_tokens_counter=0,
+            disagg_prefill_bootstrap_queue=None,
+            get_num_allocatable_reqs=lambda *args, **kwargs: 1,
+            get_prefill_adder_class=lambda: lambda *args, **kwargs: adder,
+            page_size=1,
+            tree_cache=SimpleNamespace(buffer_pipeline=None),
+            token_to_kv_pool_allocator=SimpleNamespace(state_slots=None),
+            req_to_token_pool=SimpleNamespace(),
+            new_token_ratio_tracker=SimpleNamespace(current=1),
+            max_prefill_tokens=1,
+            chunked_prefill_size=1,
+            priority_scheduling_preemption_threshold=0,
+            max_prefill_bs=1,
+            max_running_requests=2,
+            tp_worker=SimpleNamespace(
+                model_runner=SimpleNamespace(
+                    attn_backend=SimpleNamespace(), lora_manager=_lora_manager(slots=2)
+                )
+            ),
+        )
+
+        with get_context().override_server_args(pp_size=2):
+            # Neither microbatch alone fills the pool. Alternating them must
+            # keep the shorter adapter draining for the waiting third adapter.
+            for running_batch in (first, second, first):
+                scheduler._get_new_batch_prefill_raw(None, running_batch)
+                self.assertFalse(
+                    scheduler.lora_drainer.can_schedule(request("short", 100))
+                )
+                self.assertFalse(
+                    scheduler.can_schedule_lora_req(
+                        waiting, {req.lora_id for req in scheduler._get_all_pp_reqs()}
+                    )
+                )
+
+            short.finished = lambda: True
+            scheduler._get_new_batch_prefill_raw(None, second)
+            self.assertTrue(
+                scheduler.can_schedule_lora_req(
+                    waiting, {req.lora_id for req in scheduler._get_all_pp_reqs()}
+                )
+            )

+class TestFetchKeepsLiveAdapters(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_evicts_an_idle_adapter_instead_of_a_live_one(self):
+        """LRU alone would evict "live": it was used least recently."""
+        manager = _lora_manager(slots=2)
+        manager.fetch_new_loras({"live"})
+        manager.fetch_new_loras({"idle"})
+
+        manager.fetch_new_loras({"new"}, pp_loras={"live"})

+        self.assertEqual(set(manager.memory_pool.uid_to_buffer_id), {"live", "new"})

+    def test_still_loads_the_batch_when_live_adapters_do_not_fit(self):
+        manager = _lora_manager(slots=2)
+        manager.fetch_new_loras({"a", "b"})
+
+        manager.fetch_new_loras({"c", "d"}, pp_loras={"a", "b"})

+        self.assertEqual(set(manager.memory_pool.uid_to_buffer_id), {"c", "d"})

+# A 4-layer model on two PP stages: the first holds embed_tokens and layers 0-1,
+# the last holds layers 2-3 and lm_head.
+NUM_LAYERS, HIDDEN, VOCAB, RANK = 4, 8, 32, 2
+
+
+def _stage_pool(layers, embed_tokens=False, lm_head=False, added_tokens_size=0):
+    config = SimpleNamespace(
+        num_hidden_layers=NUM_LAYERS, hidden_size=HIDDEN, vocab_size=VOCAB
+    )
+    dims = {"embed_tokens": (VOCAB, HIDDEN), "lm_head": (HIDDEN, VOCAB)}
+    base_model = torch.nn.Linear(HIDDEN, HIDDEN)
+    base_model.config = config
+    base_model.get_hidden_dim = lambda name, _: dims.get(name, (HIDDEN, HIDDEN))
+    with get_parallel().override(tp_size=1, tp_rank=0, attn_tp_size=1):
+        return LoRAMemoryPool(
+            base_hf_config=config,
+            max_loras_per_batch=1,
+            dtype=torch.float32,
+            max_lora_rank=RANK,
+            target_modules={"o_proj", "embed_tokens", "lm_head"},
+            base_model=base_model,
+            eviction_policy="lru",
+            lora_added_tokens_size=added_tokens_size,
+            lora_layer_ids=layers,
+            has_embed_tokens_lora=embed_tokens,
+            has_lm_head_lora=lm_head,
+        )
+
+
+def _allocated(pool):
+    return {
+        "layers": [i for i, b in enumerate(pool.A_buffer["o_proj"]) if b is not None],
+        "embed_tokens": bool(pool.embedding_A_buffer),
+        "lm_head": bool(pool.lm_head_A_buffer),
+    }
+
+
+def _o_proj_weight(layer):
+    return torch.full((RANK, HIDDEN), float(layer))
+
+
+def _full_adapter():
+    layers = []
+    for i in range(NUM_LAYERS):
+        o_proj = f"model.layers.{i}.self_attn.o_proj"
+        weights = {
+            f"{o_proj}.lora_A.weight": _o_proj_weight(i),
+            f"{o_proj}.lora_B.weight": torch.ones(HIDDEN, RANK),
+        }
+        layers.append(SimpleNamespace(weights=weights, pinned_weights={}))
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        config=SimpleNamespace(r=RANK, lora_added_tokens_size=0),
+        layers=layers,
+        embedding_layers={
+            "model.embed_tokens.lora_embedding_A": torch.ones(RANK, VOCAB),
+            "model.embed_tokens.lora_embedding_B": torch.ones(HIDDEN, RANK),
+        },
+        added_tokens_embeddings={},
+        pinned_embedding_layers={},
+        pinned_added_tokens_embeddings={},
+    )
+
+
+def _load_into_mem_pool(pool, uid, adapter):
+    no_slicing = SimpleNamespace(
+        slice_lora_a_weights=lambda w: w, slice_lora_b_weights=lambda w: w
+    )
+    lora_modules = [{} for _ in range(NUM_LAYERS)]
+    for i in pool.lora_layer_ids:
+        lora_modules[i][f"model.layers.{i}.self_attn.o_proj"] = no_slicing
+    pool.load_lora_weight_to_buffer(uid, 0, adapter, lora_modules, None, None)
+
+
+class TestStagePool(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_each_stage_allocates_and_loads_only_its_part(self):
+        first = _stage_pool(layers=[0, 1], embed_tokens=True)
+        last = _stage_pool(layers=[2, 3], lm_head=True, added_tokens_size=1)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            _allocated(first),
+            {"layers": [0, 1], "embed_tokens": True, "lm_head": False},
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            _allocated(last), {"layers": [2, 3], "embed_tokens": False, "lm_head": True}
+        )
+        self.assertIsNone(last.get_embedding_tensor("added_tokens", LoRAType.LORA_A))
+
+        # The last stage must skip the adapter's layers 0-1 and embed_tokens weights.
+        _load_into_mem_pool(last, "adapter", _full_adapter())
+        for i in (2, 3):
+            self.assertTrue(
+                torch.equal(last.A_buffer["o_proj"][i][0], _o_proj_weight(i))
+            )
+
+        # Handing the slot to the base model zeroes it.
+        _load_into_mem_pool(last, None, None)
+        for i in (2, 3):
+            self.assertFalse(last.A_buffer["o_proj"][i][0].any())
+
